user.title: Sign in to Home Connect
user.description: Open [this address]({url}) and sign in with the account the app uses. The browser ends on a Home Connect page meant for a phone, which may show a QR code; ignore what it shows. Copy the whole address out of the address bar and paste it below.

data_description.code: The whole address, not just part of it. It is only good once and only for a few minutes.
data_description.transport: Through the Home Connect cloud, or straight to the appliances on your own network. Signing in is needed either way: the account is the only place the key to an appliance is kept.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to Home Connect again
reauth_confirm.description: The stored sign in has stopped working. Open [this address]({url}), sign in with the same account, and copy the whole address the browser ends on out of the address bar.

data_description.code: The whole address, not just part of it. It is only good once and only for a few minutes.

reconfigure.title: How to reach the appliances
reconfigure.description: Change this to move an account already set up between the cloud and the local network. Nothing else changes and there is no need to sign in again.

data_description.transport: Local control needs each appliance to be on the same network as Home Assistant and to be announcing itself on it.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Home Connect. Check your connection and try again.
error.invalid_auth: That address was not accepted. A code is only good once and only for a few minutes, so open the address above again and sign in afresh.
error.unknown: Something unexpected went wrong. Check the log for details.

abort.already_configured: This account is already set up.
abort.already_in_progress: Another appliance has already asked. One sign in covers every appliance on the account.
abort.unique_id_mismatch: That is a different account. Sign in with the one this entry was set up for.
abort.reconfigure_successful: Changed. The appliances are being reached the new way now.

never_answered.title: {name} is not talking to Home Connect
never_answered.description:
The Home Connect cloud lists this {type} on your account but says it has never connected, so there is nothing to read from it and nothing to set on it. Home Assistant cannot do anything about that from here: the appliance is the thing that has to reach the cloud.

Three things to check on the appliance, in this order.

Whether it is switched on. Several kinds, hobs above all, only hold a connection to the cloud while they are in use. One sitting switched off keeps just enough of its network module awake to answer the app over the local network, so it looks perfectly healthy there while the cloud has never heard from it.

Whether it is allowed out. The Home Connect app calls that permission "Connection to server", and it decides whether the appliance may talk to the Home Connect servers at all.

What its network settings say. The app's extended network settings show the address, gateway and DNS server the appliance is using. One with no gateway or no DNS server has nowhere to send anything.

Nothing needs doing here. This notice goes away by itself once the appliance answers.
